Report_ID: Maternal iron-deficiency anaemia during pregnancy (Hb <100 g/l plus s-ferritin <15 µg/l)
Title: Iron supplementation in pregnancy: is less enough? A randomized, placebo controlled trial of low dose iron supplementation with and without heme iron
Author: Eskeland, Malterud, Ulvik & Hunskaar
Comment: Paper's criterion uses Hb <100 g/l (not <110 g/l) and is defined 'during pregnancy' rather than specifically at >=37 weeks; denominators are the randomised intention-to-treat group sizes (31+30 vs 29) since Table II gives no separate denominators. Zero events in the iron arm but 4 in placebo, so the trial is estimable (not a double-zero trial). No risk ratio was reported by the authors; the chi-squared p-values in Table II refer to the TOTAL number of treatment failures, not this criterion alone.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron supplemented (heme iron group + non-heme iron group combined, 27 mg elemental iron daily from week 20 to delivery)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: healthy pregnant women (<13 weeks gestation at enrolment, Hb 110-148 g/l)
Recruitment source: inner city maternity centre, Bergen, Norway
Outcome measurement: Number of women meeting both low-Hb and low-ferritin criteria (Table II, criterion row 1)
Outcome variable: Maternal iron-deficiency anaemia during pregnancy (Hb <100 g/l plus s-ferritin <15 µg/l)
additional_group_ns: Reported separately in Table II: heme iron group 0 events of 31 randomised; non-heme iron group 0 events of 30 randomised; these two iron arms are combined here as the single iron-containing intervention arm (61) versus placebo (29).
follow_up_timepoint: at or near term / delivery (≥37 weeks)

Title: Impact of prophylactic iron supplementation in healthy pregnant women on maternal iron status and birth outcome
Author: Falahi, Akbari, Ebrahimzade, Pourghasem Gargari
Comment: Zero events in BOTH arms at delivery (0% vs 0%) — not estimable as a risk ratio and excluded from pooling per the synthesis plan. Event counts were not printed as integers; 0% necessarily implies 0 events. Denominators taken as the randomised group sizes (n=70 iron, n=78 placebo); the paper does not state the exact number analysed at delivery (3 abortions in iron group, 1 in placebo group were mentioned in Discussion).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron (60 mg elemental iron as ferrous sulfate daily until delivery)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); zero events in both arms -- not estimable for a ratio measure (Cochrane convention: excluded from pooling, not continuity-corrected)
Participant type: Nonanemic primigravid pregnant women (Hb >110 g/L, ferritin >20 µg/L, <20 weeks gestation, age 20-35, BMI 25-30)
Recruitment source: Gynecology center, Khorramabad City, Lorestan Province, western Iran
Outcome measurement: Percentage of women with Hb < 110 g/L and ferritin < 12 µg/L at delivery
follow_up_timepoint: at or near term / delivery (≥37 weeks)

Report_ID: Maternal iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) at delivery (Hb < 110 g/L and ferritin < 12 µg/L)
Title: Efficacy and tolerability of low-dose iron supplements during pregnancy: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Makrides M, Crowther CA, Gibson RA, Gibson RS, Skeaff CM
Comment: P value reported as P < 0.005 (threshold, not exact). Denominator for IDA (198/185) differs from Hb (200/193) and ferritin (186/176) denominators because IDA required both measures.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron-supplemented group (20 mg elemental Fe/d as ferrous sulfate from 20 wk gestation until delivery)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: pregnant women (singleton or twin pregnancies, no preexisting anaemia) at 20 wk gestation
Recruitment source: Antenatal clinics, Women's & Children's Hospital, Adelaide, Australia
Outcome measurement: Number of women with IDA / number assessed at delivery
Outcome variable: Maternal iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) at delivery (Hb < 110 g/L and ferritin < 12 µg/L)
follow_up_timepoint: at or near term / delivery (≥37 weeks)

Report_ID: Maternal iron deficiency anemia at or near term (by serum ferritin criterion)
Title: Prenatal Iron Supplementation Reduces Maternal Anemia, Iron Deficiency, and Iron Deficiency Anemia in a Randomized Clinical Trial in Rural China, but Iron Deficiency Remains Widespread in Mothers and Neonates
Author: Zhao G, Xu G, Zhou M, Jiang Y, Richards B, Clark KM, Kaciroti N, Georgieff MK, Zhang Z, Tardif T, Li M, Lozoff B
Comment: P value reported as "<0.001"; recorded as 0.001 (upper bound). Denominators are final analysed Ns with outcome data.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron/folate (300 mg ferrous sulfate = 60 mg elemental iron + 0.40 mg folate daily)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: maternal nutrition / micronutrient supplementation in pregnancy
Participant type: pregnant women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies, <=20 wk gestation, age >=18 y, hemoglobin >=100 g/L
Recruitment source: first prenatal visit at Sanhe Maternity and Child Health Care Center, rural Sanhe County, Hebei Province, China
Outcome measurement: n/total n (%) of women with hemoglobin <110 g/L + SF <15 µg/L; RR (95% CI); chi-square test
Outcome variable: Maternal iron deficiency anemia at or near term (by serum ferritin criterion)
follow_up_timepoint: at or near term / delivery (≥37 weeks)

Report_ID: Maternal iron deficiency anaemia in late pregnancy (S-ferritin ≤20 μg/l + transferrin saturation <15% + Hb <110 g/l)
Title: Iron supplementation during pregnancy. Effect on iron status markers, serum erythropoietin and human placental lactogen. A placebo controlled study in 207 Danish women
Author: Milman N, Agger AO, Nielsen OJ
Comment: Event COUNTS are not reported verbatim; the paper gives only percentages per arm with stated denominators (n=63 iron, n=57 placebo). group_1_events=0 follows directly from the explicit statement "none iron deficiency anaemia" / "None of the females had both...". group_2_events=10 is derived from 17.7% of 57 (=10.1) and is corroborated by the Discussion statement "only two out of 10 females with overt iron deficiency had MCV below the chosen level". No risk ratio, confidence interval or significance test for this dichotomous outcome is reported by the authors. Not a double-zero trial (placebo arm had events).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron treated (ferrous fumarate 200 mg = 66 mg elemental iron daily from 16th week to delivery)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: healthy pregnant women with normal single pregnancy, recruited at 14-18 weeks of gestation
Outcome measurement: Percentage of women in each arm meeting all three iron-deficiency-anaemia criteria at 35-38 weeks of gestation (maximum/end-of-pregnancy value reported in abstract and Table 5)
Outcome variable: Maternal iron deficiency anaemia in late pregnancy (S-ferritin ≤20 μg/l + transferrin saturation <15% + Hb <110 g/l)
follow_up_timepoint: at or near term / delivery (≥37 weeks)
